items.title: codex_local 2026.916.1 forces sandbox_mode=workspace-write over the managed config; on AppArmor-restricted hosts every command fails while runs report succeeded
items.body:
## Summary

Starting in 2026.916.1, `adapter-codex-local` adds `-c sandbox_mode="workspace-write"` whenever `dangerouslyBypassApprovalsAndSandbox` is false. It does this even when the agent's managed `CODEX_HOME/config.toml` already sets `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"`. On 2026.831.1 the config file decided.

On hosts where bwrap cannot create a user namespace, every shell command the seat runs now fails with `bwrap: setting up uid map: Permission denied`. Ubuntu 24.04+ with `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1` is one such host, and so are many VMs.

## Why it is hard to notice

- The runs still finish as `succeeded`. Codex reports the sandbox failure only to the model, as the command result. No `command_execution` item with the bwrap error ever reaches the run log.
- The only signal outside the agent's own messages is the kernel audit log (`apparmor="DENIED" ... comm="bwrap"`).
- On our instance, two seats spent about 25 minutes after the upgrade unable to run any command, and 4 cards ended up asking the board for a disposition.

## Workaround

Pass an explicit sandbox in `extraArgs`, which the new logic respects: `["-c", "sandbox_mode=\"danger-full-access\""]`.

## Suggestion

- Respect a `sandbox_mode` already set in the managed config, or
- run a sandbox preflight (spawn `bwrap --unshare-user true`) and fail the run loudly when the sandbox cannot start, instead of letting it "succeed".

items.title: feat(bot): run Chromium sandboxed as a non-root user — clean recording frame
items.body:
## What

The meeting bot's Chromium now runs **sandboxed, as a non-root user**, instead of as root with `--no-sandbox`. The renderer gets its real namespace sandbox, and the *"You are using an unsupported command-line flag"* security banner is gone from the recording frame.

## Why

Launching the browser as **root forced `--no-sandbox`** (root can't use the Chromium sandbox), which both disabled the sandbox and painted the yellow security banner over every server-side recording. Simply removing the flag from our arg lists didn't help — Playwright's `launchPersistentContext` defaults to `chromiumSandbox: false` and injects `--no-sandbox` **itself**.

## How

- **`browser.ts`** — `chromiumSandbox: !CHROME_NO_SANDBOX`, so Playwright enables the sandbox and omits `--no-sandbox`.
- **Non-root `vexa` user** in both images (Lite + full bot). Lite drops privileges in `vexa-bot-launch` via `setpriv`; the full-bot `entrypoint.sh` re-execs itself non-root. `/app/storage/screenshots` is pre-created `vexa`-owned — the join flow's diagnostic screenshots would otherwise `EACCES` under root-owned `/app` and **abort the join**.
- **seccomp** — Chromium's namespace sandbox needs user namespaces, which the default Docker seccomp denies. The Docker and k8s runtime backends set `seccomp=unconfined` on **bot containers only** (scoped by `VEXA_BOT_CONFIG`); `make lite` sets `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` on the container.
- **The banner** — the *essential* `--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled` (anti-detection; dropping it makes Meet flag the bot) is itself a "bad flag", so we can't remove our way out. A managed policy **`CommandLineFlagSecurityWarningsEnabled=false`** (`/etc/chromium/policies/managed`) suppresses the warning with **no automation signal** — unlike `--test-type`, which correlated with Meet refusing admission.
- **Escape hatch** — `CHROME_NO_SANDBOX=1` restores the legacy root + `--no-sandbox` path for hosts that can't relax seccomp.

## Validation (live, self-hosted Lite)

- Bot joins Google Meet and records **as `vexa`** (recording files owned by `vexa`); `unshare --user` works and Chromium stays sandboxed.
- Extracted recording frames: **no `--no-sandbox`/flag banner**, and the "Microphone muted by system" / "Camera not found" Meet snackbars stay dismissed.
- Full meeting recorded end-to-end (join → record → clean finalize with `#EXT-X-ENDLIST`); recording is servable mid-meeting and the combined download stays audio/video in sync.
- Verified the escape path: with the default seccomp profile `unshare --user` is `EPERM`; unconfined, it succeeds and headless Chromium renders `rc=0`.

## Docs

`docs/changelog.d/1025-nonroot-chrome.md`, the `CHROME_NO_SANDBOX` row in `configuration.mdx`, and the `seccomp=unconfined` requirement in `deployment-lite.mdx`.

## Stacking

Stacked on **#1015** (`video-recorder`) → **#1016** (`recording-player`) — non-root only depends on `video-recorder`'s `browser-args.ts`. The cumulative diff shrinks to just the non-root commit once those merge; safe to reorder/pull in that order.

items.title: [BUG] Bash tool refused in nested user namespace since 2.1.220: apply-seccomp: write /proc/self/uid_map: Operation not permitted
items.body:
<!--
Paste-ready issue body for anthropics/claude-code#89478. Each `###` heading is a field of .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml. Lines are intentionally unwrapped for GitHub. No placeholders left to fill.

Title: [BUG] Bash tool refused since 2.1.220 when running inside an unprivileged user namespace: apply-seccomp: write /proc/self/uid_map: Operation not permitted
-->

### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this hasn't been reported yet
- [x] This is a single bug report
- [x] I am using the latest version of Claude Code (2.1.236)

### What's Wrong?

When Claude Code runs inside an unprivileged user namespace (a rootless container, or a `bwrap --unshare-user` wrapper), the Bash sandbox fails during setup and every command is refused before it runs:

```
apply-seccomp: write /proc/self/uid_map: Operation not permitted
```

This started in **2.1.220** and is still present in **2.1.236**. **2.1.212 works** in the same environment. It is model-independent — the failure happens at sandbox setup, before any tool logic runs.

The cause is a change in the bwrap arguments used by the bundled sandbox (anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime). The sandbox helper `apply-seccomp` has two ways to get `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` for its PID+mount unshare: **(a)** the caller keeps the capability for it via bwrap `--cap-add`, or **(b)** it creates its own nested user namespace and writes that namespace's `uid_map`. 2.1.220 added `--cap-drop ALL` to the secure-mode bwrap invocation, which forces path (b) — and path (b) cannot work in this environment, because `--cap-drop ALL` empties the capability **bounding set**, so the nested user namespace grants no capabilities and the map writes fail.

Binary evidence across versions (string search on the shipped executables):

| version | contains `--cap-drop` | contains `--cap-add` | Bash in a nested userns |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.1.212 | no | no | works |
| 2.1.231 | yes | no | fails |
| 2.1.236 | yes | no | fails |

No shipped version passes `--cap-add`, so path (a) is never enabled and path (b) is the only path available — which `--cap-drop ALL` simultaneously breaks.

### What Should Happen?

Bash should run, as it does on 2.1.212. Secure mode should hand `apply-seccomp` the capability it needs (`--cap-add CAP_SYS_ADMIN`) so it takes path (a), instead of relying on a nested-user-namespace bootstrap that an already-nested environment cannot perform. Failing that, the failure should be reported with the actionable message the code already has for the sibling case ("caller must provide CAP_SYS_ADMIN") rather than a bare `EPERM`.

### Error Messages/Logs

```
apply-seccomp: write /proc/self/uid_map: Operation not permitted
```

Emitted at sandbox setup, once per Bash invocation, before the command string is executed. With a mandatory sandbox (`failIfUnavailable: true`, `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false`) this becomes a hard refusal of every command.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch Claude Code inside an unprivileged user namespace, e.g.:

   ```sh
   bwrap --unshare-user --unshare-pid --dev /dev --proc /proc --ro-bind /usr /usr --ro-bind /etc /etc --symlink usr/bin /bin --symlink usr/lib /lib --symlink usr/lib64 /lib64 --bind ~/.claude ~/.claude --bind "$PWD" "$PWD" --chdir "$PWD" -- claude
   ```

2. Make the sandbox mandatory in `~/.claude/settings.json`:

   ```json
   { "sandbox": { "enabled": true, "failIfUnavailable": true, "allowUnsandboxedCommands": false } }
   ```

3. Ask Claude to run any Bash command.
4. Every command is refused with the error above, before it runs.
5. Repeat on 2.1.212 → Bash works.

The underlying mechanism reproduces without Claude Code, in a plain shell. Inside the outer namespace from step 1:

```sh
BW="bwrap --ro-bind /usr /usr --ro-bind /etc /etc --symlink usr/bin /bin --symlink usr/lib /lib --symlink usr/lib64 /lib64 --dev /dev --unshare-pid --unshare-user"

# Secure mode (what 2.1.220+ does) — no caps at all, so apply-seccomp's path (a) is impossible:
$BW --proc /proc --cap-drop ALL -- sh -c 'grep CapBnd /proc/self/status; unshare --pid --mount --fork true'
#   CapBnd: 0000000000000000
#   unshare: unshare() failed: Operation not permitted      <- falls back to the uid_map path, which then fails

# Weaker mode (and 2.1.212's shape) — caps retained, path (a) succeeds, uid_map is never written:
$BW --bind /proc /proc -- sh -c 'grep CapBnd /proc/self/status; unshare --pid --mount --fork true && echo OK'
#   CapBnd: 000001ffffffffff
#   OK

# Proposed fix — drop everything except the one capability apply-seccomp needs:
$BW --proc /proc --cap-drop ALL --cap-add CAP_SYS_ADMIN -- sh -c 'grep CapEff /proc/self/status; unshare --pid --mount --fork true && echo OK'
#   CapEff: 0000000000200000    (CAP_SYS_ADMIN only)
#   OK
```

### Claude Model

Not applicable / model-independent — the failure is at sandbox setup, before the model runs any tool. Observed with both Sonnet and Opus.

### Is this a regression?

Yes.

### Last Working Version

2.1.212

### Claude Code Version

2.1.236 (also reproduced on 2.1.220, 2.1.221, 2.1.231; `linux-x64`).

### Platform

Anthropic API

### Operating System

Other Linux — Pop!_OS 24.04 LTS, kernel `7.0.11-76070011-generic` (x86_64), bubblewrap 0.11.0. Unprivileged user namespaces are unrestricted here (`user.max_user_namespaces=2147483647`, no AppArmor `apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns` gate), so this is not the Ubuntu 24.04 LSM restriction documented in the sandbox README.

### Terminal/Shell

Other — launched via a wrapper script; terminal-independent, and reproduces headlessly.

### Additional Information

**Root cause is in the bundled sandbox**, anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime; I have filed the mechanism-level report there and cross-linked this issue. Line references are pinned to commit [`e5fb1b9`](https://github.com/anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime/commit/e5fb1b93ba61bab8e916bee7541860bbdaa612cf) (v0.0.74, current `main`).

- [`src/sandbox/linux-sandbox-utils.ts:1955`](https://github.com/anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime/blob/e5fb1b93ba61bab8e916bee7541860bbdaa612cf/src/sandbox/linux-sandbox-utils.ts#L1955) (secure mode) pushes `--unshare-user --cap-drop ALL --proc /proc`. The weaker branch at [1965](https://github.com/anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime/blob/e5fb1b93ba61bab8e916bee7541860bbdaa612cf/src/sandbox/linux-sandbox-utils.ts#L1965) pushes `--unshare-user --bind /proc /proc` — no cap drop.
- [`vendor/seccomp-src/apply-seccomp.c:685-699`](https://github.com/anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime/blob/e5fb1b93ba61bab8e916bee7541860bbdaa612cf/vendor/seccomp-src/apply-seccomp.c#L685-L699) documents the two paths, and explicitly anticipates this failure mode: path (b) "can itself fail on hosts where unprivileged user namespaces are gated by an LSM … the unshare succeeds but the new namespace grants no capabilities, so the setgroups write fails. In that case we abort: the caller must supply CAP_SYS_ADMIN."
- Same symptom, different trigger: here the new namespace grants no capabilities because `--cap-drop ALL` emptied the bounding set (measured: `CapBnd: 0000000000000000`, and `CapEff` is still `0` *inside* the freshly created user namespace), not because of an LSM.
- Path (a) is [line 709](https://github.com/anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime/blob/e5fb1b93ba61bab8e916bee7541860bbdaa612cf/vendor/seccomp-src/apply-seccomp.c#L709); the path (b) fallback is [734–746](https://github.com/anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime/blob/e5fb1b93ba61bab8e916bee7541860bbdaa612cf/vendor/seccomp-src/apply-seccomp.c#L734-L746), and the message users see is the `die()` at [743](https://github.com/anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime/blob/e5fb1b93ba61bab8e916bee7541860bbdaa612cf/vendor/seccomp-src/apply-seccomp.c#L743).

**Suggested fix:** pass `--cap-add CAP_SYS_ADMIN` alongside the existing `--cap-drop ALL` at `linux-sandbox-utils.ts:1955`, which is exactly the arrangement `apply-seccomp` was written for (its comments at [688-689](https://github.com/anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime/blob/e5fb1b93ba61bab8e916bee7541860bbdaa612cf/vendor/seccomp-src/apply-seccomp.c#L688-L689) and [834-836](https://github.com/anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime/blob/e5fb1b93ba61bab8e916bee7541860bbdaa612cf/vendor/seccomp-src/apply-seccomp.c#L834-L836) both describe a caller that uses `--cap-add`, but no shipped build passes it). Confinement of the workload is unchanged: `apply-seccomp` clears the ambient set at [837](https://github.com/anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime/blob/e5fb1b93ba61bab8e916bee7541860bbdaa612cf/vendor/seccomp-src/apply-seccomp.c#L837) and sets `PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS` at [859](https://github.com/anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime/blob/e5fb1b93ba61bab8e916bee7541860bbdaa612cf/vendor/seccomp-src/apply-seccomp.c#L859) before `execvp` at [871](https://github.com/anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime/blob/e5fb1b93ba61bab8e916bee7541860bbdaa612cf/vendor/seccomp-src/apply-seccomp.c#L871), so the sandboxed command still starts with zero effective capabilities plus the seccomp filter.

**Impact:** any deployment running Claude Code inside an unprivileged user namespace — rootless containers, nested bwrap/firejail wrappers, some CI sandboxes — loses the Bash tool entirely on 2.1.220+ when the sandbox is mandatory.

**Workaround (verified):** set `enableWeakerNestedSandbox` in `~/.claude/settings.json`. This selects the branch at line 1965, which omits `--cap-drop ALL`, so `apply-seccomp` keeps `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`, takes path (a), and never writes a nested `uid_map`:

```json
{ "sandbox": { "enabled": true, "failIfUnavailable": true, "allowUnsandboxedCommands": false, "enableWeakerNestedSandbox": true } }
```

Confirmed working on 2.1.236 in the environment described above, with the sandbox still enabled and mandatory. Note the trade-off flagged by the comments at [1941-1944](https://github.com/anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime/blob/e5fb1b93ba61bab8e916bee7541860bbdaa612cf/src/sandbox/linux-sandbox-utils.ts#L1941-L1944): this branch binds the host `/proc` instead of mounting a fresh one, so host `/proc` is visible inside the sandbox, and the capability bounding set is left intact. The `--cap-add CAP_SYS_ADMIN` fix above would be strictly narrower than this workaround. Other options are to pin 2.1.212, or to disable the inner sandbox and rely on outer isolation (`"enabled": false`, or `failIfUnavailable: false` + `allowUnsandboxedCommands: true`).

## Cross-reference

Reported upstream at anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime#498.

items.title: False bubblewrap user namespace warning on Ubuntu when outer sandbox works but nested bwrap is blocked by AppArmor

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
## Summary

Codex CLI 0.157.1 on Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS shows this startup warning:

```
⚠ Codex's Linux sandbox uses bubblewrap and needs access to create user namespaces.
```

However, bubblewrap/user namespaces work from the normal host shell, and Codex's outer bubblewrap sandbox is demonstrably working. The failure appears when a new `bwrap` is started from inside the already confined `unpriv_bwrap` sandbox, where AppArmor intentionally denies capabilities.

This makes the startup warning appear misleading in this configuration.

## Environment

- Codex CLI: 0.157.1
- Ubuntu: 24.04.4 LTS
- Architecture: x86_64
- AppArmor user namespace restriction enabled
- `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 1`
- `kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone = 1`
- Distribution AppArmor profile: `/etc/apparmor.d/bwrap-userns-restrict`

## Host bubblewrap test succeeds

From a normal shell:

```bash
time bwrap --unshare-user --unshare-net --ro-bind / / /bin/true
```

Result:

```
real 0m0.010s
user 0m0.001s
sys  0m0.009s
```

Exit status: 0.

So `/usr/bin/bwrap` can create the required user namespace from the host shell.

## Codex processes are unconfined

Host-side inspection of running Codex processes showed:

```
3218 unconfined .../app-server-daemon/releases/0.157.1-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/bin/codex app-server --listen
3283 unconfined .../app-server-daemon/releases/0.157.1-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/bin/codex app-server daemon ...
5143 unconfined .../app-server-daemon/releases/0.157.1-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/bin/codex-code-mode-host
5381 unconfined codex
```

The standalone TUI and app-server daemon are both version 0.157.1.

## Outer Codex sandbox is working

Commands executed by Codex in its normal sandbox produced:

```bash
touch /etc/codex_test
# exit 1:
# touch: cannot touch '/etc/codex_test': Read-only file system

curl -sI https://example.com
# exit 6
```

A file in the current home-directory workspace could be created, which is consistent with that directory being the writable workspace.

Inside the Codex execution environment:

```
/proc/1/attr/current
bwrap//&unpriv_bwrap (enforce)
```

So commands are actually running inside the bubblewrap/AppArmor sandbox.

## AppArmor evidence

The active Ubuntu `bwrap-userns-restrict` profile allows the first bwrap to create a user namespace, then transitions children to `unpriv_bwrap`. That child profile contains an intentional capability denial.

Kernel audit log entries when nested bwrap/unshare was attempted included:

```
apparmor="DENIED" operation="capable" class="cap"
profile="unpriv_bwrap" comm="unshare"
capability=21 capname="sys_admin"

apparmor="DENIED" operation="capable" class="cap"
profile="unpriv_bwrap" comm="bwrap"
capability=21 capname="sys_admin"
```

A later nested bwrap attempt produced the same `sys_admin` denial under `unpriv_bwrap`.

By contrast, no corresponding denial was observed for the outer bwrap that creates the working Codex sandbox.

## Observed difference

Normal host shell:

```
bwrap --unshare-user --unshare-net --ro-bind / / /bin/true
=> exit 0
```

Inside an already established Codex sandbox, attempting another bwrap results in:

```
bwrap: No permissions to create new namespace
=> exit 1
```

That nested failure is consistent with the Ubuntu AppArmor profile intentionally preventing children of bwrap from retaining capabilities.

## Expected behavior

If Codex can successfully establish and enforce its outer Linux sandbox, it should not show a startup warning implying that bubblewrap lacks access to create user namespaces merely because a nested bwrap probe is blocked by the confinement of the already-created sandbox.

Ideally the startup check should distinguish:

1. Failure to create the outer Codex sandbox, which is security relevant.
2. Failure to create another nested bwrap from inside an already confined `unpriv_bwrap` environment, which can be expected with Ubuntu's `bwrap-userns-restrict` profile.

## Actual behavior

Codex shows:

```
⚠ Codex's Linux sandbox uses bubblewrap and needs access to create user namespaces.
```

even though the outer sandbox is functioning and enforcing filesystem/network restrictions.

## Security consideration

Disabling `bwrap-userns-restrict`, globally disabling AppArmor's unprivileged user namespace restriction, or granting capabilities to `unpriv_bwrap` would weaken the host security configuration merely to remove the warning. No such workaround was applied.

It would be preferable for Codex to avoid the false/misleading warning when the outer sandbox has already been established successfully, or to make the warning describe the nested-bwrap condition accurately.

items.title: [Bug]: Linux Desktop renderer crash loop survives clean fallback markers — setuid-sandbox lane cannot create /dev/shm (ESRCH); --disable-setuid-sandbox dies with "No usable sandbox"

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

items.body:
### Summary

On this host the X11/Intel desktop app enters a renderer crash loop (`render-process-gone reason=crashed exitCode=5` → `surfacing recovery page`), and the loop **still reproduces with the fallback markers removed/clean**, i.e. it is not (only) the marker poisoning tracked in #131055. With a fresh `userData`, the lane Chromium picks by default cannot create `/dev/shm`:

```
ERROR:base/memory/platform_shared_memory_region_posix.cc:214] Creating shared memory in /dev/shm/.org.chromium.Chromium.ZkWj5Q failed: No such process (3)
ERROR:base/memory/platform_shared_memory_region_posix.cc:217] Unable to access(W_OK|X_OK) /dev/shm: No such process (3)
FATAL:base/memory/platform_shared_memory_region_posix.cc:219] This is frequently caused by incorrect permissions on /dev/shm.  Try 'sudo chmod 1777 /dev/shm' to fix.
```

`/dev/shm` is healthy for every process I can check from a shell; forcing the user-namespace lane (`--disable-setuid-sandbox`) immediately dies with `No usable sandbox!` (the #130177 signature, and here it is a true negative: `unshare --user --map-root-user true` fails on this host). The only lane that renders is `--no-sandbox` — and only when the switch arrives on the **launch command line**.

### Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Hermes Agent | `v0.22.1+233.gacc3cad (2026.9.24)`, commit `acc3cada0da86c81efc8aa6c5a291989549ca900`, branch `main`, install method `git`, `payload: bootstrap` |
| Desktop build | packaged `apps/desktop/release/linux-unpacked`, Electron `40.10.2`, `app.getVersion()` = `"0.0.0"` (confirmed by the crashpad annotation `_version=0.0.0`) |
| OS / kernel | Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, `7.0.0-38-generic` (unchanged across the last three boots) |
| Session / GPU | X11 (`DISPLAY=:0`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` empty), Intel CoffeeLake-S GT2 [UHD Graphics 630] — no NVIDIA, no Wayland |
| AppArmor | `5.0.2-0ubuntu1~26.04.1`; `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 1`, `kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone = 1`; `unshare --user --map-root-user true` → `write failed /proc/self/uid_map: Operation not permitted` |
| Sandbox helper | `chrome-sandbox` present, `-rwsr-xr-x root root` (4755) |
| /dev/shm | `tmpfs`, 3.8 G, mode `1777`, `rw,nosuid,nodev,inode64,usrquota`, 1 % used; `touch` and an 8 MB `dd` write both succeed |
| Memory | 7.7 GB RAM / 10 GB swap, no OOM events |

### The markers are not the (only) trigger here

Method: launch the packaged binary directly, with `userData` redirected to a fresh directory (`HERMES_DESKTOP_USER_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ud-…`), so all three recovery markers start absent and the boot-abort ladder cannot escalate. The ladder indeed never engaged — `grep -c 'sandbox fallback enabled' <stderr>` = 0 in every run. Same binary, same 22–25 s observation window, identical `--disable-gpu`, one variable changed per row; the count is of `platform_shared_memory_region_posix` lines and `Renderer process crashed` lines on stderr.

| argv (all with `--disable-gpu`) | `/dev/shm` FATALs | `Renderer process crashed` | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| *(none — Chromium default lane)* | 45 (earlier identical run: 645) | 14 (earlier: 214) | crash loop, main process later dies: `Trace/breakpoint trap (core dumped)` |
| `--disable-setuid-sandbox` (userns lane) | 0 | 0 | instant `FATAL:zygote_host_impl_linux.cc:128] No usable sandbox!` — 1 stderr line total |
| `--disable-dev-shm-usage` (temp-file shm, sandbox on) | 66 | 16 | still crashes; temp-file shm reduces but does not remove it |
| `--no-sandbox` | 0 | 0 | renders (window, gateway ready) |

Markers in the scratch `userData` after each run: `{"state":"ok"}` for `windows-sandbox-fallback.json`, `linux-gpu-fallback.json`, `windows-gpu-stack-cookie-fallback.json`.

Also from the default-lane run, on a host with no discrete GPU:

```
ERROR:content/browser/gpu/gpu_process_host.cc:998] GPU process launch failed: error_code=1002
FATAL:content/browser/gpu/gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:415] GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.
```

For the record, the real config dir still carries a sticky escalation written by this app: `windows-sandbox-fallback.json` = `{"state":"fallback","reason":"boot-loop","version":"0.0.0"}`. Since `app.getVersion()` is `"0.0.0"` on this packaged-from-source build, the version comparison in `windows-sandbox-fallback.ts` (`marker.version !== appVersion` → re-probe) can never fire, so the "sticky per app version, not forever" intent in that file's header comment does not hold on this install class. (Looks like #131067's `launch-build-identity.ts` covers that part — flagging it only because it composes here.)

### What recovers the app, and how

`--no-sandbox` on the **launch command line**: `hermes config set desktop.electron_flags '["--no-sandbox"]'` makes the CLI put the flag on the original argv (`hermes_cli/main_desktop.py` `_desktop_launch_options` → `config_electron_flags`), which covers the GUI launcher too, because the desktop entry is `Exec=/home/akz404/.local/bin/hermes desktop`. The app then renders normally (today: window up, `[boot] Hermes gateway is ready`, bot roster served). Survives updates, needs no root and no system-wide change.

Note the contrast that matters for the ladder design: in the pre-fix captures on this host, a launch that logged the escalation still produced the same FATALs, while the same binary renders when the switch is on the command line. That is consistent with what the #131055 thread already established about the runtime switch landing after the browser process reads its command line — so on a host like this the ladder's escalation path cannot heal the launch by itself.

### Relation to existing reports (why this is not a duplicate)

- #131055 / PR #131067 — same symptom chain and the same three log lines, but its reproduction is *marker poisoning* (second-instance/abort → sticky `--no-sandbox`), and there, resetting the marker to `ok` fixes it. Here the loop reproduces with the markers clean and with the ladder provably not engaging, and `--disable-dev-shm-usage` does not rescue it either, so the failing component is the sandboxed lane itself on this host. If that reading is wrong I would like to know which lane Chromium should have picked.
- #130177 — I reproduce its exact `No usable sandbox!` FATAL by forcing `--disable-setuid-sandbox`. On this host that is not a probe false positive: `unshare --user --map-root-user` genuinely fails, so the user-namespace lane is unavailable and Chromium falls back to the setuid helper that is installed here.
- #138277 / PR #138294 — related mechanism, opposite detection problem: the pre-`ready` probe in that PR runs in the unsandboxed main process, and on this host ordinary processes create+write+unlink in `/dev/shm` fine (`touch`, 8 MB `dd` both succeed), so the probe would pass and the temp-file fallback would never engage — while the sandboxed renderer still cannot create there (and `--disable-dev-shm-usage` alone still crashed 16 times in my run).
- #121954 — the default lane on this host also ends in `Trace/breakpoint trap (core dumped)`; possibly the same family, listed for cross-reference.

### Questions

1. On a host where AppArmor blocks unprivileged user namespaces **and** `chrome-sandbox` is installed setuid-root, is the setuid-sandbox lane expected to be able to create `/dev/shm`? If not, should the launcher treat "userns unavailable + setuid lane" as a first-class condition (and put the flag on the launch command line) instead of relying on the post-abort ladder, whose runtime switch cannot reach Chromium?
2. Is the `ESRCH` (`No such process`) on both `openat(.org.chromium.Chromium.*)` and `access("/dev/shm", W_OK|X_OK)` from inside the sandboxed child an expected signature of that lane, or does it point at a chroot/namespace detail worth fixing? The FATAL text suggests a permissions problem, which sends every reporter down the `chmod 1777` path even though `/dev/shm` is `1777` and writable here.
3. Does #131067 change anything for hosts in this class? (This host is not a user-namespace host, so the "do not escalate on userns hosts" step would not apply — but the escalation mechanism that *would* apply is the one that fails here.)

### Reproduction

```bash
cd ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/apps/desktop/release/linux-unpacked
# fresh markers, no ladder escalation, one variable per run
for f in "" "--disable-setuid-sandbox" "--disable-dev-shm-usage" "--no-sandbox"; do
  rm -rf /tmp/ud-probe; mkdir -p /tmp/ud-probe
  env HERMES_DESKTOP_USER_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ud-probe timeout 22 ./Hermes $f --disable-gpu --enable-logging=stderr > /tmp/probe.log 2>&1
  printf "flags='%s' shm_fatals=%s renderer_crashed=%s\n" "$f" \
    "$(grep -c platform_shared_memory_region_posix /tmp/probe.log)" \
    "$(grep -c 'Renderer process crashed' /tmp/probe.log)"
done
```

Observed on this host (2026-10-16): `''` → 45 / 14; `--disable-setuid-sandbox` → 0 / 0 + `No usable sandbox!`; `--disable-dev-shm-usage` → 66 / 16; `--no-sandbox` → 0 / 0.

Happy to run any probe, gather a core, or test a patched build on this host — the app has been renderable here since the flag went on the launch command line, so the host stays available for A/B work.

```
$ codex sandbox -- echo hi
bwrap: Can't mount devpts on /newroot/dev/pts: Permission denied
$ codex doctor
  ✓ sandbox      restricted fs + restricted network · approval OnRequest
```

Bare `bwrap --unshare-user --unshare-pid --unshare-net --ro-bind / /` plus:
- `--dev /dev` fails: `Can't mount devpts ... Permission denied`.
- `--proc /proc` fails: `Can't mount proc ... Permission denied`.
- `--ro-bind /dev/null FILE` fails: `Unable to remount destination ... Permission denied`.
- `--bind ~/projects ~/projects` fails: the share is virtiofs with `context=system_u:object_r:nfs_t:s0`.
- It runs only with `--dev-bind /dev /dev --bind /proc /proc` and no bind over the share.

A research pass also captured AVC denials for `comm="bwrap"` against `proc_t`, `device_t` and `nfs_t` in the VM's audit log.

**What this changes in `README.md:2424-2430`:** this settles its open item, "Nested bubblewrap is still not proven to work here", for macOS: it does not work. The README's guess at the cause, the fresh `/proc`, is only part of it. codex falls back on `/proc` by itself, but it cannot get past the SELinux denials. `doctor`'s green tick is not evidence of a working boundary, as the README already suspected.

**What happens to commands, from source, not exercised end to end:** codex 0.148.0 treats the failure as a likely sandbox denial. Under `on-request` the model then reruns with escalation, `auto_review` decides, and an approved command runs unsandboxed.

**Not yet tested:**
- whether `--security-opt label=disable` fixes it. The flag is on the invariants list (`container.args:53-55`).
- Linux and WSL hosts, where Ubuntu's `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns` may be the obstacle instead.

This also blocks #525, because Claude Code's sandbox makes the same bubblewrap mounts.

**Fix:** add an image test that runs `codex sandbox -- true` and asserts it succeeds. It is red on macOS today, and would stay meaningful where `doctor` isn't. Then decide between changing the container's SELinux posture and documenting that macOS students have no codex sandbox.

items.title: runc create fails without /proc when capabilities are empty
items.body:
### Description

`runc create` fails for an OCI bundle with an empty `mounts` list when all five process capability sets are explicitly empty. The failure occurs before the workload starts, while runc tries to open `/proc/sys/kernel/cap_last_cap` inside the container rootfs.

I reproduced this with a minimized `/bin/true` workload. runc failed 5/5 times with the same error. The same bundle succeeded 5/5 times with crun 1.19.1.0.0.0.47-1713-dirty and youki 0.6.0. None of the runs timed out or reached a resource limit.

As a control, I added only a private `/proc` mount. runc then succeeded 5/5 times. Since an OCI configuration does not require a `/proc` mount and the capability sets may be empty, I expected runc to accept the original bundle as well.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Run this script as a user allowed to create user namespaces:

```bash

rootfs="$bundle/rootfs"

awk '/=> \// {print $3} /^[[:space:]]*\// {print $1}' |
```

I expected runc create to accept the original configuration without requiring /proc/sys/kernel/cap_last_cap in the container rootfs.

runc 1.3.4

items.title: kernel: one module builds the macOS and Linux sandboxes and says when neither can run

labels.name: code
labels.description: Work type code, proven by tests

items.body:
Stage 0, CT4. Spec: `specs/2026-10-17-stage-0-foundation.md`.

**Blocked on D18**; written for the recommended answer. Rewrite it if Aarmen picks otherwise.

## Type
code

## Goal
A keyless module, `crivo.kernel.sandbox`, turns a "view" into a wrapped command:
- the view lists what a kernel may read, the one folder it may write, its socket folder and its working directory;
- on macOS it wraps the command in `sandbox-exec` with a deny-default Seatbelt profile;
- on Linux it wraps it in `bwrap`.

It can say, with a reason, when neither works on this machine. CI exercises both.

## Context
- Stage 0 dependencies: none.
- Plan 0d "Containment v1 without Docker"; D18 (this row **cannot start** until Aarmen answers it); D18c, D18d; inventory P0r.
- Checked on this Mac today (scratch profiles, not repo code):
  - **The profile that worked:** `(deny default)` with `process-exec`, `process-fork`, `signal (target same-sandbox)` and `sysctl-read`; reads allowed broadly, then denied under `/Users`, `/Volumes` and `/private/var/folders`, then re-allowed for the roots; `file-read-metadata` only on the roots' parent folders; writes only to the write root, the socket folder and `/dev/null`; network only for unix sockets in the socket folder; mach-lookup only for `com.apple.system.opendirectoryd.libinfo`. The supervisor, kernel, pandas, pyarrow and matplotlib all ran under it.
  - **Loopback rule:** `(allow network* (local ip "localhost:*"))` lets connects to any host through. Do not use it.
  - **Allow-default profiles** leave LaunchServices reachable. The log shows the deny-default profile denying `com.apple.lsd.*` and `coreservicesd`, but `/usr/bin/open -R /tmp` still exited 0 inside it. That is unexplained; the test below must settle it.
- bubblewrap (its docs): `--unshare-all` (user, ipc, pid, net, uts, cgroup), `--die-with-parent`, and `--new-session` (needed against TIOCSTI, CVE-2017-5226). `--unshare-net` gives a private loopback. A clone EPERM means user namespaces are blocked: Ubuntu 24.04 does this by default (`kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1`).

## Files
- `src/crivo/kernel/sandbox.py` (new)
- `tests/test_sandbox.py` (new, test-writer), `tests/conftest.py` (the `sandbox` marker, test-writer)
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (Linux: install bubblewrap, lift the restriction)
- `docs/API-CONTRACT.md` (a short "Kernel sandbox" section: backends, what a view allows)

## Steps
1. `@dataclass(frozen=True) class View: read_roots: tuple[Path, ...]; write_root: Path; ipc_dir: Path; cwd: Path; deny_names: tuple[str, ...] = (".env", ".env.*", ".git")`.
   - `View.for_python()` adds `sys.prefix`, `sys.base_prefix`, every `site.getsitepackages()` entry and the folder holding the `crivo` package.
2. `root_error(path) -> str | None`: refuse `/` and `Path.home()`, the same rule as `mcp_server._root_error`.
3. `seatbelt_profile(view) -> str`: the profile above.
   - Deny names inside roots by regex, `(deny file-read* (regex ...))`, placed after the allows.
   - Paths are escaped and resolved with `realpath`, since `/tmp` is `/private/tmp` on macOS.
4. `bwrap_argv(view) -> list[str]`:
   - `--unshare-all --die-with-parent --new-session`;
   - `--ro-bind /usr /usr`, plus `--ro-bind-try` for `/lib`, `/lib64`, `/bin`, `/sbin` and `/etc`;
   - `--proc /proc --dev /dev --tmpfs /tmp`;
   - `--ro-bind` each read root at its own path;
   - for each deny name found under the roots at start (a bounded `os.walk`, depth 4): a file gets `--ro-bind /dev/null <file>`, a folder gets `--tmpfs <dir>`;
   - `--bind` the write root and the socket folder;
   - `--chdir <cwd>`.
5. `wrap(argv, view) -> list[str]`: macOS gives `["sandbox-exec", "-p", profile, *argv]`, Linux gives `["bwrap", *bwrap_argv(view), "--", *argv]`.
6. `backend() -> tuple[str | None, str]`: run `wrap(["/bin/sh", "-c", "exit 0"], <a probe view in a temp dir>)` once per process and cache the result.
   - Return `("seatbelt", "")`, `("bwrap", "")`, or `(None, reason)`, where the reason is the first stderr line plus a hint.
   - On Linux, an EPERM or "uid map" error names the Ubuntu 24.04 restriction and points to SECURITY.md.
7. `kernel_env(view, base: dict) -> dict`: `base` with `HOME`, `TMPDIR`, `IPYTHONDIR`, `MPLCONFIGDIR`, `JUPYTER_RUNTIME_DIR` and `XDG_CACHE_HOME` pointed under `view.write_root`, plus `CRIVO_KERNEL_IPC_DIR`.
8. CI, Linux job only, before the tests: `sudo apt-get install -y bubblewrap` and `sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0`. That is a throwaway VM, so the sysctl's cost lands on nobody.
9. The `sandbox` marker in `conftest.py` skips when `backend()` is None, unless `CI` is set, in which case the test fails.

## Done when
- [ ] Unit tests on both OSes: the profile and argv contain the roots, the deny names and the write root, and never `localhost` in a network rule; `root_error` refuses `/` and home.
- [ ] `sandbox`-marked tests on the host OS's backend: a wrapped `/bin/cat` of a file outside the roots fails, inside a root reads, and a `.env` inside a root fails.
- [ ] A wrapped Python one-liner fails to connect to `192.0.2.1:443` and to a listener the test opens on the host's loopback.
- [ ] A wrapped write to a root fails, and to the write root succeeds.
- [ ] On macOS, `/usr/bin/open -g -j -a TextEdit` exits non-zero from inside, and no TextEdit process appears.
- [ ] `uv run pytest tests/test_sandbox.py -q` passes locally on macOS, and CI is green on `ubuntu-latest` and `macos-latest` with these tests running, not skipped.
- [ ] `uv run pytest -q` and `uv run ruff check .` pass.

## Measurement
None.

## Out of scope
- Running the kernel inside it (CT5 (#190)).
- Landlock, a microVM, Windows (Stage 5).
- A network proxy with a domain allowlist.

items.title: Run locally installed harness CLIs from the host for Dapr tasks
items.body:
## Goal
Keep Dapr as the workflow orchestrator while a launcher-managed host runner invokes the harness CLI the user installed on the machine where they are working. The CLI runs natively under the logged-in user's account, using that CLI's normal local setup and authentication; it is not installed or pinned in the worker as the required execution model.

## Trust model
Host execution is intentionally unsandboxed. The harness and child tools have the user's normal filesystem, process, and network permissions, not just access to the registered project or task workspace. Require explicit host-mode opt-in and show a clear full-permissions warning before execution. A per-project MyForge capability authorizes Dapr-to-runner requests only; it is not a provider credential, Dapr token, or sandbox.

## Requirements
- Keep Dapr as the durable workflow orchestrator and use a narrow typed harness-runner interface.
- Invoke only a configured, locally installed CLI; do not accept arbitrary commands or caller-supplied host paths.
- Bind requests and results to the registered project, run, task, attempt, and accepted base revision. Preserve existing validation, checkpoint, and Git integration.
- Define a local Dapr-to-runner transport and workspace/result handoff that do not expose a general host listener or trust unverified workspace changes.
- Preserve the user's normal CLI authentication while keeping MyForge/Dapr service tokens and the runner capability out of the harness environment.
- Support readiness, status, cancellation, cleanup, capability rotation/revocation, and clear errors for missing or incompatible local CLIs.
- Never silently switch execution modes. Qualify native invocation, transport, process cleanup, paths, and authentication on each supported host OS.

## Acceptance
Tests cover project and attempt authorization, invalid/revoked capabilities, path/command rejection, workspace result validation, cancellation/cleanup, secret redaction, explicit opt-in and warning behavior, and supported host-platform compatibility. Update the canonical feature contract, roadmap, user documentation, and changelog as implementation proceeds.

items.title: The outer sandbox's Landlock refusal names Linux 6.12 on a 7.0 host where Landlock is disabled (Proxmox VE LXC)
items.body:
On the host used for #339's M0 baseline, the outer sandbox can't be enforced, and AutoForge's refusal doesn't say why. The kernel is Linux 7.0, but the refusal reads like a version problem: "the kernel's Landlock ABI is unavailable; the abstract-socket scope needs ABI 6 (Linux 6.12) with Landlock enabled". Probed directly, Landlock returns `EOPNOTSUPP`, which `landlock_create_ruleset(2)` documents as built into the kernel but disabled at boot. Because of this, the 60 real-backend sandbox tests skip on this host; CI's `sandbox` job runs them.

## What happens

- `_landlock_abi` (`src/autoforge/sandbox_bwrap.py:204-212`) asks the kernel for its Landlock ABI version and returns `max(abi, 0)`, so the errno is dropped. Landlock disabled at boot (`EOPNOTSUPP`) and no Landlock syscall at all (`ENOSYS`, from a kernel without it or a seccomp filter) both become "unavailable" in the refusal (`:245-250`). An ABI below 6 is reported by number. All three cases name the same requirement, "the Landlock abstract-socket scope (Landlock ABI 6, Linux 6.12 or later)" (`:597`), which `doctor` and the documentation also use.
- On this host, `landlock_create_ruleset(NULL, 0, LANDLOCK_CREATE_RULESET_VERSION)` returns −1 with `EOPNOTSUPP` (95).
- The host is an LXC container (`systemd-detect-virt` reports `lxc`) on a Proxmox VE kernel, `7.0.14-20-pve`. `/sys/kernel/security` isn't mounted in the container, so the boot LSM list can't be read from inside it. The container also runs under a seccomp filter (`Seccomp: 2` in `/proc/self/status`). So I can't tell from here whether the cause is the Proxmox host's boot `lsm=` list or the container.
- The other requirements I could check from inside the container are present: bwrap 0.12.0 with `--overlay`, and unprivileged user and PID namespaces (`unshare` and `bwrap --unshare-user --unshare-pid` both succeed). I didn't check the session keyring. The probe stops at the first requirement it finds missing, so enabling Landlock could expose another one.

## Evidence

- 60 real-backend cases in `tests/test_sandbox_bwrap.py`, `tests/test_sandbox_parity.py` and `tests/test_sandbox_routing.py` skipped with the refusal above in every local run: M0's runs, the six full-suite runs of #345's A/B, and a literal `make check`.
- `docs/compatibility.md:167` names the requirement "Landlock ABI 6 with Landlock enabled: Linux 6.12 or later". `:174` lists "a kernel before 6.12 …, or Landlock disabled" as unsupported. The page doesn't mention containers.

## Impact

AutoForge behaves correctly here. With no outer sandbox, `sandbox.mode: required` refuses every launch. `preferred` falls back to logical isolation, visibly, in LOCAL, and refuses in REMOTE. The cost is diagnosis: an operator on a 7.0 kernel is told about Linux 6.12 and has to work out alone that Landlock is disabled, and where to enable it. For development, sandbox changes can't be validated on such a host, so CI's `sandbox` job is the only place the 60 cases run.

## Desired outcome

When the kernel's answer distinguishes the cases, the refusal and `doctor` say which one applies: Landlock disabled at boot, absent, or an ABI that is too old. Once someone verifies what is needed on LXC containers under Proxmox VE, `docs/compatibility.md` records it.

Two questions are open:

- Is enabling Landlock in the Proxmox host's boot `lsm=` list enough for it to work inside this container?
- If so, should this host then run the 60 cases?

## Summary

This is the initial implementation of FrankensteinCentral, a personal life-OS dashboard built as a microservices architecture. It provides a unified hub for managing finances, schedules, fitness, tasks, and other life domains through specialized sub-apps coordinated by an AI assistant manager.

## Key Changes

**Core Architecture**
- FastAPI-based microservices gateway with 15+ specialized sub-apps (Gmail, Schedule, Budget, Firefly, Plex, Vault, etc.)
- PostgreSQL-backed services for persistent state (core, assistant, budget, schedule, tasks, deals, finance, fitness, networth)
- Docker Compose orchestration with health checks and service discovery
- Stateless read-only clients for external services (Firefly III, Plex, Vaultwarden)

**Frontend**
- Dual-mode UI: "Lounge" (dashboard overview) and "Command Center" (today's focus screen)
- Interactive app detail modals with live health status
- Calendar views (week/month) for schedule management
- Focus timer, quick capture, and command palette (Cmd/Ctrl-K)
- Real-time clock and dynamic data refresh

**Assistant Service**
- Manager agent ("Bones") that orchestrates across sub-apps
- Specialized worker agents (Posty for email, Cal for calendar, etc.) with themed UI
- Briefing generation from cross-app data synthesis
- Telegram/SMS notification support for digest delivery
- Automatic sync with configurable intervals

**Financial Layer**
- Budget engine with paycheck-cycle awareness (pure, deterministic calculations)
- Net worth tracking with Firefly III integration
- Monthly budget tracking with spend-vs-limit guidance
- Safe-per-day projections and month-end forecasting

**Deployment & Operations**
- Production-only deployment boundary (review/production separation)

- Comprehensive verification script for live deployment health checks

**Testing & Quality**

**Documentation**

items.title: feat(sandbox): add FUSE image support (TKAI-521)
items.body:
## Decision

Ship Debian Bookworm `fuse3=3.14.0-4` for tool compatibility. Set `fusermount3` to mode `0755 root:root` and do not use setuid mounts.

Root in `unshare --user --map-root-user --mount` owns the nested mount namespace. It can use FUSE without giving UID 1500 mount authority in the outer namespace. The smoke uses `umount` and leaves `user_allow_other` disabled.

## Changes

* Pin `fuse3` and `fuse-overlayfs`.
* Validate package versions, tool modes, and optional FUSE device identity and mode.
* Use `--check-only` in Kubernetes preflight. This path never mounts FUSE or blocks k3s on a live smoke.
* Run the full 30-second smoke before the Docker consumer selects `fuse-overlayfs`.
* Warn and retain the `vfs` fallback if the Docker-side smoke fails.
* Test absent-device skip, mocked mount operations, cleanup ordering, timeout handling, mutations, and CI wiring.
* Document FUSE character device `10:229` and the non-setuid security posture.

No provider manifest change is needed. The RuntimeClass injects the OCI device.

## Rollout

1. Deploy this image. The absent-device path remains a successful skip.
2. Grant the device on one canary node with [test-agents-infra#49](https://github.com/tkhq/test-agents-infra/pull/49).
3. Confirm a real `PASS: FUSE mount smoke` in a fresh canary sandbox.
4. Apply infrastructure PR #49 fleet-wide.

A later rollout can add `VALET_REQUIRE_FUSE=1` as a fail-closed ratchet after canary validation.

## Validation

* Sandbox image build and package checks: passed.
* FUSE smoke tests and mutation tests: passed.
* Shell syntax, ShellCheck, cgroup, user namespace, and Kubernetes shell suites: passed.
* `pnpm typecheck`: passed.
* Docs lint: passed.
* `make e2e`: blocked because `make` is absent in this sandbox. The earlier container fallback was OOM-killed.

items.title: [Bug]: `scripts/desktop-update/repro.sh gate` is not hermetic — userns-dependent expectation, result-file race, and real desktop notifications from the fake-home run
items.body:
> **Disclosure — AI-authored report.** This issue was compiled and written by an AI agent (Hermes Agent, model `deepseek-v4.1-flash` via provider `opencode-go`) running on the reporter's machine, at that owner's request. Every command and output below was executed on that machine by the agent and is pasted unedited; the machine owner reviewed this before it was posted. The human owner is the reporter of record; the analysis and wording are the agent's.

Found while reproducing #94703 / the false-skew gate decision on a Bazzite (ostree) host. Product behavior in all three cases is correct — these are harness issues, filed separately so they don't muddy that thread.

Environment: Bazzite 44 (Fedora Atomic/ostree, `/home` → `/var/home`), x86_64, kernel 7.2.3-ogc3.1.fc44, Hermes v0.21.1 `8c74118c` (git install), Node v26.8.1.

## 1. The "sandbox not root/setuid" row assumes user namespaces are unavailable

```console
$ bash scripts/desktop-update/repro.sh gate
ok   appimage (not under unpacked) -> skew
ok   sibling-prefix dir not fooled -> skew
ok   no chrome-sandbox (namespace) -> relaunch
FAIL sandbox not root/setuid -> relaunch (want manual)
ok   opt-out: --sandbox-fallback -> relaunch
ok   opt-out: --no-sandbox launch arg -> relaunch
...
```

`repro.sh:114-115` touches a non-root, non-setuid `chrome-sandbox` and expects `manual`. But `linux_gate` probes the namespace sandbox *before* that arm (`posix.sh:333`):

```bash
if unshare --user --map-root-user true 2>/dev/null; then GATE=relaunch; return; fi
```

On hosts where that probe succeeds the gate correctly returns `relaunch`, so the row fails. Confirmed here:

```console
$ unshare --user --map-root-user true && echo ok
ok
```

Suggested fix: make the expectation host-derived — probe in the test the same way the gate does and assert the matching value (or explicitly force the branch, e.g. by running the row in an environment where the userns probe fails).

## 2. The result-JSON row races the detached hand-off

`repro.sh:122-128` runs the orchestrator against `$QHOME/hermes-agent` and reads `$QHOME/.hermes-update-result.json` on the next line. The orchestrator re-execs itself detached (`posix.sh:671-673`: `os.setsid()` + `os.execve` and the parent returns immediately), so the result file is written by the detached child, ~2s later:

```console
FAIL result JSON escaping
Traceback (most recent call last):
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/tmp/hermes-gate-test.41788/qhome/.hermes-update-result.json'
```

Waiting for the file shows the escaping is correct — so this is a race, not an escaping bug:

```console
$ # same invocation, then wait for the file
{"ok":false,"exit_code":3,"manual":false,"message":"Update aborted: /tmp/hg2.nr6U/qhome/hermes-agent/venv/bin/hermes is missing. The install needs repair (run the Hermes installer or hermes doctor).","branch":"evil\"branch\\n$(x)","finished_at":1789123256}
branch raw: 'evil"branch\\n$(x)' ok: False   # parses back exactly
```

Suggested fix: poll for the result file with a bounded timeout before asserting.

## 3. The fake-home run still fires real desktop notifications

Runs 1 and 2 point `--install-root` at a temp fixture (`$QHOME/hermes-agent`), and the script derives `HERMES_HOME` from its parent, so all durable state lands under the fixture — good. But `notify_fallback` (`posix.sh:130`) is **not** scoped to the real home: the abort publishes `manual/error` and pops a live `notify-send` notification on the developer's desktop:

> **Hermes update** — Update aborted: /tmp/hg2.nr6U/qhome/hermes-agent/venv/bin/hermes is missing. The install needs repair (run the Hermes installer or hermes doctor).

That is a real notification about a fixture that does not exist, shown to whoever is at the machine — during `repro.sh gate` itself and during any manual replay of the row. `--no-ui` suppresses the shim but not this.

Suggested fix: a `--no-notify` flag (or fold it into `--no-ui`), and have the harness pass it, so a test run never reaches the user's notification daemon.

## Reproduction

```bash
cd ~/.hermes/hermes-agent
bash scripts/desktop-update/repro.sh gate          # items 1 and 2
```

Item 3 shows up as a desktop notification while that runs.

## Parent

Split out of #342 (Provider PID namespace isolation: wrap provider spawn with unshare) so the doctor-warning surface can land as its own PR, separate from the wrap/init/signal-forwarding implementation.

- [ ] Test coverage exercising `doctor`'s output with the probe forced unavailable.

## Blocked by

#342 — needs the cached unshare-availability probe that #342 introduces; this issue can't land before that probe exists.

items.title: `IO.appPath` fails when `/proc` belongs to another PID namespace
items.body:
### Prerequisites

<!-- Please put an X between the brackets as you perform the following steps: -->

* [x] Check that your issue is not already filed:
      https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/issues
* [x] Reduce the issue to a minimal, self-contained, reproducible test case.
      Avoid dependencies to Mathlib or Batteries.
* [ ] Test your test case against the latest nightly release, for example on
      https://live.lean-lang.org/#project=lean-nightly
      (You can also use the settings there to switch to “Lean nightly”)

### Description

On Linux, `lean_io_app_path` (`src/runtime/io.cpp`) reads `/proc/<getpid()>/exe`. In a PID namespace without its own `/proc` mount, `getpid()` returns the PID inside the namespace, while `/proc` lists the PIDs of the parent namespace. The path then names another process or none, `readlink` fails, and every tool that needs `IO.appPath` fails, including `lean` and `lake`.

### Context

Sandboxes and rootless containers often run processes in a PID namespace without remounting `/proc`. In such a sandbox, `lean --version` fails while other tools work.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `unshare --user --map-root-user --pid --fork lean --version`

**Expected behavior:** Lean prints its version.

**Actual behavior:** `error: failed to locate application`

### Versions

Lean (version 4.31.0, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, commit 68218e876d2a38b1985b8590fff244a83c321783, Release)
Linux 7.2.9

The code on master is unchanged.

### Additional Information

`/proc/self/exe` resolves correctly in this setup, because the kernel resolves `self` in the namespace of the `/proc` mount. Reading it instead fixes the problem:

```cpp
if (readlink("/proc/self/exe", dest, PATH_MAX - 1) == -1) {
```

As a workaround, an `LD_PRELOAD` shim can redirect `readlink("/proc/<getpid()>/exe")` to `/proc/self/exe`.
